title: A smooth algebra is a retract of a relative global complete intersection smooth over it
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there are integers $n,c\ge0$ and polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that, writing $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $C=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/J$: (1) $C=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]; (2) the conormal module $J/J^2$, a $C$-module, is a free $C$-module with basis the classes $f_1\bmod J^2,\dots,f_c\bmod J^2$; (3) there are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\sigma:A\to C$ and $\pi:C\to A$ with $\pi\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_A$ such that $C$, an $A$-algebra via $\sigma$, is a smooth $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection, line 567) and its proof (lines 580-588: Lemma 07CE lemma-improve-presentation gives A -> C with retraction; Algebra Lemma 07CF lemma-huber gives the presentation C = R[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) with the f_i mapping to a basis of J/J^2; fibre dimension n - c by Algebra Lemma 00SC lemma-lci). Stacks states 07CG for a syntomic ring map R -> A; this node is its case R -> A smooth (a smooth ring map is syntomic, Algebra Lemma 00TA lemma-smooth-syntomic), the only case used; clause (2) is the property of the presentation chosen in the proof, stated because Lemma 07CH uses it (the sequence 0 -> (+) C f_j -> (+) C dx_i).

proof.text: (The algebra $C_0$ with retraction and a presentation of free conormal module.) By [lem-weil-pbc-improve-presentation-smooth-conormal-free] applied to the smooth $R$-algebra $A$ there are an $A$-algebra $C_0$ with $A\to C_0$ smooth, an $A$-algebra map $\rho:C_0\to A$ with $\rho\circ(A\to C_0)=\mathrm{id}_A$, and a surjective $R$-algebra map $R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to C_0$ whose kernel $I$ has $I/I^2$ free over $C_0$. Since $R\to A$ and $A\to C_0$ are smooth, $R\to C_0$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2); in particular $C_0$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra (condition (i) of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection), line 578 ('Apply Lemma 07CE to get A -> C') and lines 582-583 (R -> C is a composition of a syntomic and a smooth ring map; here both are smooth)

proof.text: (The presentation with conormal basis; clause (2).) By [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-free-presentation-basis] (Stacks 07CF) applied to the finitely presented $R$-algebra $S=C_0$ and the presentation of step 1, there are $n,c\ge0$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\psi:C:=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/J\xrightarrow{\sim}C_0$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, such that the $C$-module $J/J^2$ is free with basis $f_1\bmod J^2,\dots,f_c\bmod J^2$. This is clause (2). Moreover $R\to C$ is smooth: it is $R\to C_0$ followed by the $R$-algebra isomorphism $\psi^{-1}$, and the three conditions of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] (finite presentation, $H_1(L_{C/R})=0$, $\Omega_{C/R}$ finite projective) are carried by $\psi$ to the same conditions for $C_0$, since the canonical presentation, the naive cotangent complex and $\Omega$ of $C$ are mapped isomorphically onto those of $C_0$ by $\psi$ (they are defined from the $R$-algebra structure alone).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection), lines 579-580 ('By Algebra, Lemma 07CF we can write C = R[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) with f_i mapping to a basis of J/J^2'), with Algebra Lemma Tag 07CF (lemma-huber, algebra.tex line 36520)

proof.text: (The maps $\sigma,\pi$; clause (3).) Put $\sigma=\psi^{-1}\circ(A\to C_0):A\to C$ and $\pi=\rho\circ\psi:C\to A$, homomorphisms of $R$-algebras (all maps are $R$-algebra maps, $A\to C_0$ and $\rho$ being $A$-algebra maps). Then $\pi\circ\sigma=\rho\circ\psi\circ\psi^{-1}\circ(A\to C_0)=\rho\circ(A\to C_0)=\mathrm{id}_A$. With $C$ an $A$-algebra via $\sigma$, $\psi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $C\to C_0$ (since $\psi\circ\sigma=(A\to C_0)$), so, exactly as in step 2 with $A$ in place of $R$, the smoothness of $A\to C_0$ (step 1) gives that $C$ is a smooth $A$-algebra via $\sigma$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. This is clause (3).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection), lines 568-570 ('a smooth R-algebra map A -> C with a retraction'), transported along the isomorphism of step 2

proof.text: (The rank of $\Omega_{C/R}$ at every point.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] to $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, the ideal $J$, $C=P/J$ and $a=1$ ($C_1=C$ is smooth over $R$ by step 2): $J/J^2\oplus\Omega_{C/R}\cong C^{\oplus n}$ as $C$-modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. By step 2, $J/J^2\cong C^{\oplus c}$, so $\Omega_{C/R}\oplus C^{\oplus c}\cong C^{\oplus n}$. Let $Q\subset C$ be a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(Q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; applying $-\otimes_C\kappa(Q)$, which commutes with finite direct sums, gives $(\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C\kappa(Q))\oplus\kappa(Q)^{c}\cong\kappa(Q)^{n}$, so $\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C\kappa(Q)$ is a $\kappa(Q)$-vector space of dimension $n-c$ (in particular $n\ge c$ if $C\neq0$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 606-617 (the split sequence 0 -> (+) C f_j -> (+) C dx_i -> Omega_{C/R} -> 0 for this C); used here in place of Algebra Lemma 00SC (see proof_origin)

proof.text: (Every point of a fibre has local dimension $n-c$.) Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $T=C\otimes_R k$ the fibre ring, a $k$-algebra via $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$, generated as a $k$-algebra by the finitely many elements $\bar x_i\otimes1$ (as $C$ is generated over $R$ by the $\bar x_i$). (i) $k\to T$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1) (step 2), hence smooth at every prime $\mathfrak n\subset T$ (take $g=1$ in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]). (ii) $\Omega_{T/k}\cong T\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}$ as $T$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change]. For a prime $\mathfrak n\subset T$ with inverse image $Q\subset C$, the map $C\to T\to\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ factors through $\kappa(Q)$, so $\Omega_{T/k}\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak n)\cong\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C\kappa(\mathfrak n)\cong(\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C\kappa(Q))\otimes_{\kappa(Q)}\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ has $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$-dimension $n-c$ by step 4. (iii) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials], applied to the finitely generated $k$-algebra $T$ smooth at $\mathfrak n$, the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at the point $\mathfrak n$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is $\dim_{\mathfrak n}(\operatorname{Spec}T)=n-c$, for every prime $\mathfrak n$ of $T$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection), lines 584-586 ('The dimension of the fibres is n - c by Algebra, Lemma 00SC'); for smooth fibres the dimension at a point is the rank of Omega, Algebra Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field)

proof.text: (The fibres have dimension $n-c$; clause (1).) Let $\mathfrak p$, $T$ be as in step 5 with $T\neq0$, so $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is $\sup_{\mathfrak n}\dim_{\mathfrak n}(\operatorname{Spec}T)$, a supremum of the nonempty family of values all equal to $n-c$ (step 5), hence equals $n-c$. As $T=(R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c))\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is exactly the fibre ring in [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], $C=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$. This is clause (1), and with steps 2 and 3 the lemma is proved.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_retract_relative_global_complete_intersection (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Smooth R A] : ∃ (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionPresentation f ∧ (∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin c) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).Cotangent, ∀ j : Fin c, b j = (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).toCotangent ⟨f j, Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self j)⟩) ∧ (∃ (σ : A →ₐ[R] (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))) (π : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) →ₐ[R] A), π.comp σ = AlgHom.id R A ∧ ∃ (_ : Algebra A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))), (Algebra.ofId A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))).toRingHom = σ.toRingHom ∧ Smooth A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))
